rl.title: Earlier: RL fit check on R1s-SD (35B), it fits with little room
rl.intro: Three training steps of 32 attempts each on the real model, same Terminal-Bench 2 tasks in Prime sandboxes. 8 H200 GPUs on Hugging Face ($40/h): 4 run the model, 4 train it.
rl.note: Training memory peaks at ~134 of 140 GB per GPU and stays flat from step to step. Copying expert choices from the model server to the trainer works: the mismatch is ~0.001, half the 9B test's. The trainer does 10K tokens/s; collecting attempts is the slow part. 66 min, ~$44. A 50-step run would be ~$360-450, over the nightly budget: your call.

qwen.title: Qwen3.8-27B on your 3090: speed
qwen.intro: New engine (TensorFold) with a small draft model that guesses several words ahead; the big model checks every guess, so its answers don't change.
qwen.context: Context: now stored in 4 bits (mixed with a fixed rotation first so rare large values don't wreck precision). The window is the model's full 262K tokens, up from 80K this morning; a 132K-token prompt ran with recall right, in 23.8 GB, at full speed (chat 103–114, code 144–147 tok/s). Intelligence check: predictions drift KL 0.002–0.006 from 16-bit, perplexity within 0.5%; 8-bit drifted less (0.0003–0.0008) but only fits 144K.
qwen.next: Done on your 3090: 102 chat / 143-192 code tok/s, full 262K window in 4-bit, math gap closed at medium effort. As an agent in prime_agent, untrained (full-precision on a rented H200): 33 of 60 vs R1s-SD's 31, a tie on solves, but it finishes in half the turns, never thinks itself into the reply cap, and follows prime_agent's tool rules without coaching (39 of 47 runs vs 3 of 54).

next_text: In progress: a purpose-built long-context attention kernel. Alone it takes attention per layer from 239 to 136 us at 20K context and 838 to 441 us at 100K (~6 ms a round less at 100K), with drafted rows bit-identical to serial ones. Now checking it inside the model (20K-context decode, drafted vs serial). Next lever after it: the 4-bit matmul kernel (~10%).
headline_text: Qwen 27B speed on your 3090, now in the server: your daily setup (4-bit cache, full 262K window) went 169 → 183 tok/s on code and 117 → 126 on chat, with answers identical to one-word-at-a-time decoding. Turn it on with TENSORFOLD_ROWS=8 TENSORFOLD_GRAPHS=1. With 20K tokens of context it's 158 vs 141 for TensorFold's default.

pilot.title: RL on R1s-SD, pilot + continuation (24 steps): small drift, no go on the full run
pilot.intro: Pilot 12 steps from base, continuation 12 more from the pilot's weights with GitHub blocked and 60-min attempts. Held-out: same 20 tasks x 3 tries, one counting rule for all three.
rows: Practice tasks solved per task (30-min scale)
1 in pilot (OCaml download) · 0 with GitHub blocked
pilot.note: Lost attempts stayed high: Prime sandbox shutdowns (not retried: pi reports them as harness errors) and timeouts even at 60 min. If RL continues, the better test is the same setup in prime_agent, where R1s-SD follows the tool rules in 3 of 54 runs, so it has room to learn.
